title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models

### The Breakthrough
Long-WAM expands visual history for causal world‑action models by pretraining video foundations autoregressively, enabling a context window up to 19.2 s and raising RoboCasa GR‑1 success from 63.3 % to 78.7 % while keeping inference latency under ~107 ms on RTX 5090, and runs on real robots such as Unitree G1 and YAM.

### The Caveats
The study reports a single 19.2 s context length without any ablation of shorter or intermediate windows, so the claimed advantage of scaling visual history is demonstrated only for that one setting.

## Agentic RSR: Real-to-Sim-to-Real via Scene Reconstruction

### The Breakthrough
Agentic RSR jointly reconstructs a metric‑scaled scene from a workspace video, trains a policy in MuJoCo, and executes it on hardware, achieving 80 % of simulation success rate across 18 scenes with reconstruction errors of 0.1057 mm depth MAE and 0.699 SSIM.

### The Caveats
The paper reports 80 % transfer fidelity but provides no comparison to existing sim‑to‑real or scene‑reconstruction baselines, so it’s unclear whether the approach actually improves over prior methods.

## Walking Robotic Hand Crawls on Fingertips

### The Breakthrough
Researchers equipped a commercial hand with a Raspberry Pi Zero backpack and trained RL policies that use per‑finger target positions and asymmetric penalties as virtual springs, enabling the hand to crawl up to 9 cm/s on 14 surface types, turn, right itself, and push a cube to targets.

### The Caveats
The demo offers no comparison to prior walking‑hand systems, leaving its claimed advantage unverified.

## Factorized Tactile Representation for Sim-to-Real Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
The factorized tactile framework separates geometry, force distribution, and temporal change, feeding them to a Tactile Gated Policy that attains sub‑mm contact localization, 1.69 N force‑tracking error on unseen shapes, and a 35 % boost in real‑world peg‑insertion success versus an unfactorized baseline.

### The Caveats
The work provides no ablation of the geometry, force‑distribution, and temporal factors, so it’s unclear which component actually accounts for the reported improvements.

## RoboPrompt: Steering Robot Policies with Sparse Human Input

### The Breakthrough
RoboPrompt adds a lightweight module that maps sparse human cues into draft actions in the diffusion policy’s noise space, then refines them with the base policy, improving task success by up to 21.3 % and cutting human interventions by up to 81.9 % after a few DAgger‑style iterations.

### The Caveats
The approach is tested only in simulation on three tasks and three policies, with no real‑world robot experiments, so its claimed real‑world deployability is unproven.

## LichtFeld Studio: Native C++ Gaussian Splatting Tool

### The Breakthrough
LichtFeld Studio bundles the full Gaussian splatting pipeline—training, interactive rendering, Gaussian selection editing, and multi‑format export—in a native C++23/CUDA app with a Python plugin system, enabling responsive performance on NVIDIA GPUs for dense 3‑D scene mapping.

### The Caveats
The tool’s claimed responsive performance is unsupported, as no quantitative benchmarks or robot‑hardware tests are provided.

## NVIDIA NeMo Gym: Scalable LLM Agent Evaluation Library

### The Breakthrough
NeMo Gym introduces Environment Servers that manage session lifecycle and token‑level trajectory capture for thousands of concurrent sandboxed environments, allowing exact replay and debugging of LLM agents at scale.

### The Caveats
The library’s claim of reproducible, scalable evaluation is unsupported, as the release provides no empirical results or benchmark comparisons to any baseline.

## Microrobots Startup Aims for AI-Designed Microrobots

### The Breakthrough
The startup proposes to use AI‑driven generative design and learning‑based control to engineer sub‑millimeter microrobots, aiming to automate morphology optimization and behavior synthesis that are traditionally manual.

### The Caveats
The startup’s claim rests on no prototype or real‑world testing, so its AI‑driven microrobot vision remains unverified.

### Priority
Long-WAM shows a clear path to immediate real‑world impact by scaling visual context for world‑action models while staying within real‑time constraints.

### One action
Try extending the visual history window in your own world‑action pipeline (e.g., start with a 5‑second context) and benchmark the effect on task success.
